_comment: Curriculum order. The map order teaches the economy: each map's payout tier is what affords the marker that the NEXT map's skill requires.
_order: The curriculum, ordered by engagement distance: Speedball 16, Dustline 18.48, Urban 27, Woods 38.72, Holdfast 45.76 metres -- each map is the next step out, and MapsSpec asserts the ordering holds against the declared bands. Dustline, Woods and Holdfast were rescaled to 88% on 2026-09-07 and their bands moved with them; Speedball and Urban were left at full size because shrinking them inverted the way they punish trading. See each map's _scale note.

palette._note: Saturated, strong silhouettes, 0-255 RGB. Surfaces are no longer uniformly flat plastic -- WorldBuilder maps each key to a material (grass, sand, concrete, timber, slate) and inflatables get a vinyl sheen -- but the rule that cover reads darker than ground, and bots read as the most saturated thing on screen, still governs every value here.
palette._undeclared: brush, stone, containerRust, gravel and trail were all in use and declared nowhere, so each fell back to concrete grey. brush/stone/containerRust were thickets, outcrops and a rusted screen on Woods, Holdfast and Dustline -- treelines rendering as pale grey boxes. gravel and trail are the ground markings on all four of those fields: every freight lane, market street and valley path was being drawn in concrete instead of gravel or dirt. WorldBuilder passes those two their own material explicitly, so only the colour was wrong -- which is exactly why nothing caught it.

assembly._note: Nav edges are not hand-listed. The builder links any two nav nodes within navLinkRadiusMetres whose connecting segment is not blocked by a cover volume. Hand-authoring 80 edges per map is how maps stop getting edited.

lighting._comment: Look tuning. The palette stays saturated and the silhouettes stay strong; what changed is that the light is doing work. Future technology gives real-time shadows and light bounce, atmosphere gives distance haze so a 70 m sightline in Woods reads as far away, and a little bloom sells the gloss on the vinyl.

default._clouds: Volumetric clouds, parented to Terrain by Match/Atmosphere. Cover is how much of the sky is occupied, density how solid each cloud reads. This is the largest change available to a Roblox sky without uploading an asset -- without it the sky is a flat gradient with no scale and no source for the light. Per-field, because an overcast deck over Speedball greys out the only palette that field has.

speedball._note: Tournament field, high sun, no weather. Crisp and flat-lit so the netting reads and the bunkers keep their colour -- this is the one field where the paint is the whole palette. Almost no haze: at a 16 m band there is no distance to sell and haze would only grey out the thing you are shooting at.

dustline._note:
Late afternoon in a freight yard, sun low and coming through dust. The warmest field by a distance: sand, rust and long shadows off the containers.

The dust is in the COLOUR and the GLARE, not in the density. It was authored at haze 1.5 first and the spec caught it -- a yard with an 18 m engagement band cannot carry more haze than the 27 m market quarter without greying out the thing you are aiming at. Looking west down a lane still costs you something; it costs you glare rather than visibility.

urban._note: Mid-morning in the market quarter. The coolest, cleanest light in the set: concrete, shade under the awnings, and enough contrast to read a silhouette on a roofline at 27 m. Deliberately the plainest profile -- this field's character is its geometry, not its weather.

woods._note: Early morning under a canopy. Green-shifted, damp, with the sun low enough to come through the trunks in shafts -- the highest sunRays in the set, which is what a treeline is for. Haze is up because a 39 m band needs the far end of the field to fade rather than end.

holdfast._note: Cold light over a wide valley, late in the day. The dimmest field allowed and the haziest: at a 46 m band the far keep should be a shape in the air rather than a crisp object, and that haze is doing the work a 200 m field cannot do on its own. Blue-grey throughout so the two keeps read as stone.

lighting._perMap:
Each field gets its own hour and its own air. They were all rendering under one profile -- the same 15:20 sun, the same haze -- which made five places with five themes read as one place with five layouts.

Two rules constrain every value here. BRIGHTNESS stays in a narrow band (2.35 to 2.70) because a bot has to read as the most saturated thing on screen on every field, and a dim field breaks that before it looks moody. HAZE scales with the field's own engagement band: distance haze sells scale on Holdfast at 46 m and simply muddies Speedball at 16 m, where there is no distance to sell.

depthOfField stays off everywhere on purpose. Far blur looks wonderful and costs you the target you were about to shoot, which on an aim trainer is the one trade that is never worth making.
